title: Adding perpendicular velocities
caption: The boat heads north at 4.0 m s⁻¹ while the river carries it east at 3.0 m s⁻¹. Placed tip to tail, the two velocities give the velocity over the ground: 5.0 m s⁻¹ at 37° east of north, not 7 m s⁻¹, because vectors add by direction as well as size.
alt: Vector triangle: a north arrow of 4.0 m/s, an east arrow of 3.0 m/s from its tip, and the resultant of 5.0 m/s from the start to the end, 37 degrees east of north.
description: The boat's own velocity, 4.0 m s⁻¹ north, is drawn up the page from the starting point.
The river's velocity, 3.0 m s⁻¹ east, is drawn from the tip of the first arrow, to the right.
The resultant runs from the start of the first arrow to the tip of the second: |v| = √(4.0² + 3.0²) = 5.0 m s⁻¹.
Its direction: tan φ = 3.0/4.0, so φ = 37° east of north.
notes: tan φ = 3.0/4.0, φ = 37° east of north
